# lvlath/go

> lvlath/go is a deterministic, contract-driven, pure-Go library for graph modeling, traversal, shortest paths, spanning trees, network flow, routing, dense matrix computation, combinatorial optimization, grid construction, reproducible fixtures, time-series alignment, exact affine exponential level smoothing, and observed Donchian range channels with explicit current-bar policy.


Maintained repository: `github.com/lvlath/go`.
Use `go get github.com/lvlath/go`; read `go.mod` for the required Go version.
The maintained implementation requires Go 1.23.4 or newer and is licensed under `AGPL-3.0-only`.

Canonical Go module: `github.com/lvlath/go`

Install with:

```bash
go get github.com/lvlath/go@latest
```


## Start here

- [Repository README](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/README.md): Overview and working entry points.
- [Go module](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/go.mod): Module path and Go requirement.
- [Tutorial](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/docs/TUTORIAL.md): Package selection and composition.
- [Go reference](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go): Published API documentation; check the selected version.

## Important usage rules:

- Read source and package documentation at the selected repository/module version. `pkg.go.dev` may describe a different published version; do not infer new symbols from an older release page. Do not invent exported functions, options, fields, or result methods.
- Build graph topology with `core.Graph`; use algorithm packages for computation and `matrix` for dense numeric artifacts.
- Deterministic ordering and tie-breaking are observable API behavior where documented.
- Public sentinel errors are checked with `errors.Is`; never match error strings.
- Non-trivial algorithms return inspectable evidence such as paths, predecessor maps, cycle witnesses, trees, cuts, residual graphs, tours, alignments, or matrices.
- Numeric meanings are package-specific. Do not treat `0`, `+Inf`, `NaN`, a missing edge, an unreachable state, and an untracked witness as interchangeable.
- Preserve caller ownership and aliasing rules documented by each package. Do not mutate returned or retained values unless the API explicitly permits it.
- Prefer explicit options over inferred policy. Never silently substitute a weaker algorithm, memory mode, matching policy, topology interpretation, or numeric encoding.

## Package-selection guide:

- Use `core` for deterministic, thread-safe graph topology and explicit directed/weighted/loop/multi-edge/mixed-edge capabilities.
- Use `builder` for deterministic fixtures and reproducible graph construction.
- Use `bfs` for unweighted shortest-hop traversal, paths, layers, and weak components.
- Use `dfs` for depth-first forests, finish order, cycle witnesses, and topological sorting.
- Use `dijkstra` for non-negative weighted single-source shortest paths.
- Use `mst` for minimum spanning trees or explicitly requested spanning forests.
- Use `flow` for max-flow/min-cut computation and residual-network evidence.
- Use `gridgraph` to generate lattice graphs for routing and traversal workloads.
- Use `matrix` for dense matrices, graph adapters, metric closure, algebra, statistics, and factorization workflows.
- Use `tsp` for exact, approximate, heuristic, and local-search tour construction under documented assumptions.
- Use `dtw` for deterministic scalar, multivariate, or cost-matrix dynamic time warping.
- Use `ema.ComputeSMA` / `ComputeFirst` for owning, index-aligned smoothed levels with an explicit period, or `NewSMA` / `NewFirst` and `Stream.Push(ctx,x)` for recoverable streaming. Canonical `Compute` and `New` accept full `ema.Options`.
- Use `atr.ComputePeriod` / `NewPeriod` for an explicit observation horizon, or `ComputeDefault` / `NewDefault` to explicitly select `DefaultPeriod=14`. Canonical Compute/New retain Options; Options{} is invalid. ATR measures range, not smoothed price levels.
- Use `donchian.ComputeIncludeCurrent(ctx,high,low,period)` for a finalized-bar overlay or `ComputeExcludeCurrent` for a preceding-range comparison. Canonical `Compute` accepts Options. No default period, Stream, or Snapshot exists.

## Critical semantic boundaries:

- `bfs`: discovery/visited state is not the same as processing order.
- `dfs`: discovery order is not finish order and is not automatically a topological order.
- `dijkstra`: unknown target, known unreachable target, disabled path tracking, and missing path evidence are distinct states.
- `mst`: a disconnected graph has no single spanning tree; forest behavior must be requested explicitly.
- `flow`: a scalar maximum-flow value is incomplete when the caller needs residual or cut evidence.
- `matrix`: classic adjacency may use `0` for absence; zero-preserving weighted adjacency uses finite `0` for a real zero-weight edge and `+Inf` for absence. All-zero weighted graphs require explicit zero-weight preservation.
- `matrix`: metric closure stores derived all-pairs distances and must not be exported as if those distances were literal graph edges.
- `tsp`: exactness, metric assumptions, matching policy, time limits, and incumbent optimality are explicit contracts.
- `dtw`: alignment cost and recovered alignment path are different result products; path recovery depends on memory policy.
- `ema`: require `1 <= Period < MaxInt`; there is no default period. Finite negative values and subnormals are valid. Nil/empty slices succeed after context/options checks; a short SMA history has +0/false entries.
- `ema`: exact represented-input SMA sum/P at index P-1, or first-value seeding at index zero; then one nearest-even rounding of `((P-1)*previous+2*x)/(P+1)`. Do not use rounded alpha, an overflowing difference, a floating numerator, or MACD's private kernel. P1 returns x except that -0 becomes +0.
- `ema`: check error before Valid. Failed Push returns Value{} and changes no state; successful warmup also returns Value{} but advances Count. Result.IsNil checks pointer presence, not readiness. Result copies share slice backing arrays.
- `ema`: Snapshot Version=1, Algorithm="ema/affine-rn/v1"; restore only into a constructed stream with matching Options. Warmup SeedSum is exact signed decimal in 2^-1074 units, at most 660 bytes and bounded by Count*MaxBinary64Units. Outside SMA warmup it is "0". Current is finite and zero-canonical.
- `ema`: one owner per Stream, no internal locks or retained history. Caller owns cadence, duplicates, corrections, source cursor, checkpoint authentication, and lossless numeric serialization. EMA is not ATR, a full Keltner channel, a prediction interval, or a trading/safety decision.
- `ema`: Push uses fixed O(34) arithmetic and no internal heap allocation. Compute performs two linear passes and owns O(n) output; Snapshot may allocate its decimal seed string. Keep persistence, logging, and custom context costs outside Push claims.

- `atr`: all finite signed H/L/C prices are allowed if low<=close<=high. Nonfinite input is ErrNonFinite; invalid finite geometry is ErrBar. Mixed nil/nonempty columns give ErrNilInput; other unequal lengths give ErrShape. Empty and short histories succeed after validation.
- `atr`: TR0=RN64(H0-L0), no synthetic previous close. TR stays available during warmup; Valid belongs only to ATR. The first ATR is RN64(exactSum(roundedTR[0:P])/P), followed by RN64(((P-1)*previousATR+TR)/P). P1 is bitwise identity. No EMA coefficient, float alpha, clamp, or warmup TR masking.
- `atr`: failed Compute returns nil; failed Push returns Value{} and changes no state. Result.IsNil is a pointer check. One Stream has one owner. NewPeriod/NewDefault delegate to New; no extra options, seed modes, or implicit default period exist.
- `atr`: Snapshot Version=1, Algorithm="atr/wilder-rn/v1". PreviousClose and exact unsigned SeedSum preserve continuation; canonical decimal is bounded to 660 bytes and Count*MaxBinary64Units. Warmup Current is +0; mature Current is finite nonnegative, including either zero sign. Restore is structural validation, not authentication.
- `atr`: source identity/revision/offset, candle finality, correction replay, channel composition, and alert policy belong to the caller. Do not implement NATR, positions, stops, or division by ATR in the package. A ready zero is a valid measurement. Push has fixed O(34) work with no internal heap allocation; JSON, logging, and custom contexts are separate.


- `donchian`: include window [i-P+1,i], first ready P-1; exclude [i-P,i-1], first ready P. All positive int periods including MaxInt are valid; Options{} is invalid. P counts observations, not calendar days. Include is causal after bar availability, but is not a prior-bar threshold.
- `donchian`: finite signed H/L with high>=low; latest equal extrema retain input bits. Middle rounds the exact boundary mean to nearest-even without destructive overflow/underflow. Exact zero becomes +0; negative nonzero means may round to -0. A finite Middle does not guarantee a finite width or ratio.
- `donchian`: context -> options -> shape -> complete nonfinite scan -> first finite ErrBar -> computation/publication. Nil/nonempty matches both ErrShape and ErrNilInput. Even excluded or masked rows are validated; every error returns nil. Do not copy ATR's per-index error order.
- `donchian`: Result owns aligned Upper/Middle/Lower/Valid; false masks imply +0 payloads, ready zeros remain valid. Empty inputs return non-nil empty channels. IsNil is only pointer presence. Result carries no Options or source provenance.
- `donchian`: O(n) total work, O(n) output, O(min(P,n)) workspace. Entirely masked histories allocate no rings. Individual inserts can pop O(P); polling is phase-local, not hard real-time. Packed numerical channels are disjoint cap-limited views; keeping one retains the array, and struct copies are shallow. No runtime OOM recovery is promised.
- `donchian`: callers govern time grids, closed bars, source revisions, close validity, chunk overlap, corrections and execution. Prior ATR normalization uses a ready ATR[i-1] and explicit finite arithmetic; no inferred epsilon or fill. All tests are external; fixed fixtures/oracles are in test_helper_test.go and five complete scenarios are in example_test.go.

## Package documentation:

- [core](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/core): Deterministic graph topology, capabilities, identity, ownership, and concurrency rules.
- [builder](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/builder): Deterministic graph builders and reproducible fixtures.
- [bfs](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/bfs): Breadth-first traversal, shortest-hop paths, layers, components, filters, hooks, and partial results.
- [dfs](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/dfs): Depth-first traversal, finish order, cycle witnesses, and topological sorting.
- [dijkstra](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/dijkstra): Non-negative weighted shortest paths, path witnesses, cutoffs, and unreachable-state publication.
- [mst](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/mst): Prim/Kruskal minimum spanning trees and explicit forest behavior.
- [flow](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/flow): Ford-Fulkerson, Edmonds-Karp, Dinic, residual graphs, and cut evidence.
- [gridgraph](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/gridgraph): Deterministic two-dimensional lattice graph generation.
- [matrix](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/matrix): Dense matrices, graph adapters, zero-weight policy, metric closure, algebra, statistics, and factorizations.
- [tsp](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/tsp): Exact, approximate, heuristic, and local-search tours with explicit assumptions and stopping policy.
- [dtw](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/dtw): Dynamic time warping, windows, slope penalties, memory modes, costs, and optional path recovery.
- [ema](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/ema): Exact affine exponential levels, explicit seed policies, Values/Valid, transactional streaming and bounded continuation. Use the source links below when the selected published version predates the package.
- [atr](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/atr): Exact True Range and Wilder ATR, signed candles, independent readiness, named period facades, and lossless single-owner continuation. Check the selected published version.
- [donchian](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/donchian): Observed rolling ranges, explicit current-bar inclusion, exact midpoint and aligned readiness. Use repository source when the selected published version predates the package.

## Detailed guides:

- [Core guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/CORE.md): Graph contracts, topology, identity, ownership, concurrency, and operational examples.
- [BFS guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/BFS.md): Queue semantics, discovery versus processing, paths, components, and pitfalls.
- [DFS guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/DFS.md): Discovery/finish semantics, cycles, DAG validation, and topological ordering.
- [Dijkstra guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/DIJKSTRA.md): Input domain, unreachable states, witnesses, policy, and complexity.
- [MST guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/MST.md): Prim/Kruskal, strict tree versus forest behavior, and disconnected inputs.
- [Flow guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/FLOW.md): Augmenting paths, residual networks, cuts, and algorithm selection.
- [Matrix guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/MATRICES.md): Dense storage, numeric policy, zero-weight preservation, graph adapters, APSP, statistics, and factorizations.
- [TSP guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/TSP.md): Exactness, approximation assumptions, local search, limits, and result interpretation.
- [DTW guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/DTW.md): Alignment cost, path recovery, windows, penalties, and memory modes.
- [Grid graph guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/GRID_GRAPH.md): Lattice construction, connectivity, obstacles, and routing scenarios.
- [EMA guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/EMA.md): Correct rounding, seed and error tables, lossless warmup replay, complete programs, complexity, and pitfalls.
- [ATR guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/ATR.md): Exact range arithmetic, phase/error tables, prior-baseline review, source provenance and replay.
- [Donchian guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/DONCHIAN.md): Window/error tables, finite-domain midpoint proof, deque bounds, ownership, complete usage and source-timing pitfalls.
- [Documentation routes](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/README.md): Learning routes, package-owned contracts, and Donchian's actual standard-library imports.

## Numerical representations and alignment:

- [Matrix contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/matrix/doc.go): Dense storage, numeric policies and graph representations.
- [Matrix API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/matrix/api.go): Implemented constructors and operations.
- [DTW](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/dtw/doc.go): Sequence alignment, cost models, windows and memory policies.
- [EMA contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/ema/doc.go): Numeric domain, readiness, errors, ownership, cancellation, and snapshot ABI.
- [EMA API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/ema/api.go): Compute/New and the four named seed wrappers; no implicit period defaults.
- [EMA types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/ema/types.go): Options, Result.IsNil, Value, and Snapshot fields.
- [ATR API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/atr/api.go): Canonical Compute/New and the four period/default wrappers.
- [ATR charter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/atr/doc.go): Signed domain, exact rounding, masks, ownership, cancellation and snapshot ABI.
- [ATR types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/atr/types.go): Options, Result.IsNil, scalar Value, and Snapshot.
- [Donchian charter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/donchian/doc.go): Windows, domain, masks, errors, ownership and cancellation.
- [Donchian API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/donchian/api.go): Compute and the two explicit include/exclude-current wrappers; no hidden defaults.
- [Donchian types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/donchian/types.go): Options, owning Result and pointer-only IsNil.

## Examples and verification:

- [Runnable examples](https://github.com/lvlath/go/tree/main/examples): Cross-package executable scenarios using the implemented public API.
- [Package tests](https://github.com/lvlath/go): Validation, medium, edge, adversarial, deterministic, and concurrency tests live beside each package.
- [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/lvlath/go/actions): Continuous integration status and workflow history.
- [Codecov](https://codecov.io/github/lvlath/go): Repository coverage reporting.
- [EMA executable scenarios](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/ema/example_test.go): Centerline, tick-noise admission, seed failover, prior-baseline incident review, rejected telemetry, and extreme cancellation. Run `go test ./ema -run Example -count=1` from the repository root.
- [EMA rational oracle](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/ema/test_helper_test.go): Independent represented-input reference arithmetic and typed comparison helpers; tests use `package ema_test`.
- [EMA benchmarks](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/ema/bench_test.go): Batch sizes 1e3/1e5/1e6 and periods 14/64/512; separate steady-state, warmup, and adversarial Push regimes. Report the actual toolchain and machine; no universal timing guarantee.
- [ATR executable scenarios](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/atr/example_test.go): Frozen vendor-source audit, prior-baseline review, warmup failover, rejected-row retry, signed spreads and ready zeros. Run `go test ./atr -run Example -count=1`.
- [ATR oracle and fixtures](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/atr/test_helper_test.go): External tests, independent math/big.Rat arithmetic and offline source parsing; no production test hooks.
- [ATR CSV replay](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/examples/atr/main.go): Bounded stdin CSV, typed checkpoint plus source cursor, and suffix bit parity.
- [Donchian executable scenarios](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/donchian/example_test.go): Current-range report, prior-20 audit, 10/50 compression, signed spreads and feed quarantine. Run `go test ./donchian -run '^Example' -count=1 -v`.
- [Donchian oracles and fixture provenance](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/donchian/test_helper_test.go): Independent direct-window/rational arithmetic and frozen or engineered data; no live requests.
- [Donchian benchmarks](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/donchian/bench_test.go): Size/period grid, masked MaxInt, full rings, equal eviction, pop bursts and wrappers; setup outside timing.
